unresolved.issue: Authentication stage models TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED as an entry_from_previous with exit via REQUEST_AUTHORIZED back to task_execution for secondary credential flows. However, spec section 7.6 states secondary credentials are obtained out-of-band and provided via subsequent message/send, which flows through the interruption stage (AUTH_REQUIRED → WORKING). No listed boundary supports a task_execution → authentication crossing; the secondary auth loop appears to be modeled redundantly across authentication and interruption stages.

Termination stage contains non-terminal state 'submitted' (lowercase, source D-6-6-012) listed in entry_from_previous, but task_execution and initiation use 'TASK_STATE_SUBMITTED' (uppercase). Naming inconsistency prevents confident pairing. No state named 'submitted' exists in task_execution or initiation.

Termination stage contains non-terminal state 'STREAM_OPEN' (source D-3-1-038) listed in entry_from_previous with transition to STREAM_CLOSED. Task_execution uses 'STREAM_STATE_OPEN' (different name). No state named 'STREAM_OPEN' exists in task_execution. Name mismatch prevents resolution.

Interruption stage contains STREAM_STATE_OPEN with no incoming transitions (flagged as unreachable in B1). Stream may carry over from task_execution when task enters interrupted state, but task_execution already models stream closure on interrupted states via STREAM_ACTIVE → STREAM_CLOSED (guard includes INPUT_REQUIRED, AUTH_REQUIRED). Ambiguous whether a separate inter-stage stream carry-over is required or is redundant with intra-stage stream closure.

gaps.issue: All candidate exit states in task_execution are semantic_type terminal or have outgoing intra-stage transitions. Terminal states (TASK_STATE_COMPLETED, TASK_STATE_FAILED, TASK_STATE_CANCELED, TASK_STATE_REJECTED, STREAM_CLOSED) satisfy the no-outgoing-transitions criterion but violate the non-terminal exit state heuristic. Terminal-to-terminal crossings were defined as best-available resolution.

Termination stage contains TASK_STATE_WORKING as a non-terminal entry state (listed in entry_from_previous) with transitions to COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELED, REJECTED. These duplicate transitions already present in task_execution. task_execution.TASK_STATE_WORKING has outgoing intra-stage transitions, preventing it from serving as a strict exit candidate. No clean inter-stage connection resolved.

Termination stage contains STREAM_ACTIVE as a non-terminal entry state (listed in entry_from_previous) with transition to STREAM_CLOSED. Could map from task_execution.STREAM_ACTIVE but that state has outgoing intra-stage transitions (self-loop and to STREAM_CLOSED). Overlapping modeling prevents clean boundary resolution.

Termination stage contains STREAM_STATE_OPEN as a non-terminal entry state (listed in entry_from_previous) with transition to STREAM_STATE_CLOSED. Could map from task_execution.STREAM_STATE_OPEN but that state has outgoing intra-stage transitions. Additionally, initiation and interruption stages also contain STREAM_STATE_OPEN, creating a three-way ambiguity.

Initiation stage has terminal states (TASK_STATE_REJECTED, STREAM_CLOSED) representing termination outcomes for tasks rejected or message-only streams closed before reaching task_execution. No boundary is defined between initiation and termination in the stage order, so these terminal states have no inter-stage path to the termination phase.
